# Build: always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Build "Always fill every slot: when slots are free, run independent steps of running builds in parallel across them, and auto-queue pending builds" (always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are) is complete.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account hulu0241 for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Extraordinary care for expansion: placeholders everywhere, open registries, nothing in a build may constrain later scaling.
- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Stay in this one session; no sub-agents; keep every step within its cap; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
- Watch live: when you start on a screen or element, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "<what you are changing>"` so the live preview follows you.
- Code, comments, commits, PRs and docs stay clean and professional. In what you say to Brett you are Amber: short, blunt, lead with the result, plain phone-readable lines, say what broke and what it cost.
- Done means merged and working (done-means-merged@1, Nov 17 2026, Brett: "We asked you to build it. You should do whatever you have to do to build it, period."): never stop on a failure. A crash, red CI, a clash, a failed push or a stalled step is something you fix and retry with a different approach, not a reason to end the session: merge main in, fix the failing check, regenerate fixtures, redo the step. Never mark a build built or complete yourself: every step ticked means landing; the server sets landed only once the PR is merged and CI is green on the merge commit, and complete only once the feature verify passed (the builds store refuses anything else). If you truly cannot go on, write a build note saying what broke and what you tried; the server retries on its ladder (retry, fix, fresh session, another model or account) and escalates to the systems check banner and one phone push only when it runs out. Spec: `framework/spec/DONE-MEANS-MERGED.md`; check `node framework/spec/check-done-means-merged.mjs`.

steps.text: Add the step-dependency contract to builds@1. Steps get an optional `after: [stepId]` list and a `claim: {runId, slot, account, branch, at}` record. Old builds with no `after` stay sequential, so each step waits for the previous one. Update the schema, `framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs` header docs and `_claude/builds/README.md`.

Make `framework/cli/builds-store.mjs` keep `after` and `claim` on steps through normBuild and the newer-wins merge. Add a migration that leaves old steps implicitly sequential. Check for dependency cycles and for `after` ids that point at missing steps.

Add `readySteps(build)` and `claimStep` / `releaseStep` to `framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs`. A step is ready when everything in its `after` list is done and it has no live claim. Claims are model-aware (the step's pinned model) and expire after a TTL.

Add the fill-slots planner `planFill({slots, accounts, running, queue, pending, settings})` to `framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs`. It fills every free slot in this order: ready steps of running builds, then Queue builds by priority, then Pending builds when auto-queue is on. It respects the agent cap, the memory floor, per-account model limits (Fable phases only to accounts with Fable) and budget caps. It returns the list of launches with the reason for each.

Write the contract for merging parallel steps back. Each parallel step runs on branch `<build-branch>--s<n>` in its own worktree off the build branch, then merges into the build branch when done. A merge conflict releases the claim and turns the step into a sequential retry with a note. Put the spec in `framework/spec/BUILD-PARALLEL.md` and add fixtures for `readySteps`, claims and `planFill` in `framework/spec/fixtures/build-pipeline-fill.json`.

Design the step-dependency contract: add optional `dependsOn: [stepId]` and `parallel: auto|never` to build steps in build-pipeline@1 (framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs), with the rule that steps with no `dependsOn` run in order (the old behaviour), plus a pure `readySteps(build)` that returns the steps whose dependencies are all done and that touch no files another running step is touching. Update the builds@1 normaliser so the new fields are kept and not dropped.

Design the fill-slots plan as a pure function: `planFill({slots, accounts, queue, running, pending, settings})` in framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs. It returns the launches in priority order: ready steps of running builds first, then Queue builds, then (only when the owner setting is on) Pending builds that are split and have no clashes, auto-queued. Each launch respects the model per account (Fable phases go to accounts with Fable) and the per-build max-parallel and budget caps.

Add golden fixtures plus check-build-pipeline cases for readySteps and planFill: linear steps unchanged, a fan-out/fan-in DAG, a file-overlap clash held back, a Fable step with no Fable account free, auto-queue off vs on, caps reached, a priority order tie.

Store migration: give existing builds no `dependsOn` (they keep running one step at a time). Add `builds-store.mjs verify` checks for a dependsOn that points at a missing step and for dependency cycles. Version the change in the journal.

Splitter: change pipeline.mjs intake so the Opus split prompt also asks for `dependsOn` per step (default: the previous step) and `files`, and so the reply is parsed and validated with no cycles. Hand-written steps are left untouched.

Add the owner-only Claude settings `builds.fillSlots` (run independent steps in parallel, default on) and `builds.autoQueuePending` (default off; only Brett's console click changes it) plus `builds.maxParallelPerBuild` (default 3). Register them in claude-settings with their owner-only flags and help text.

Parallel step worktrees: add `pipeline.mjs` helpers that create a step worktree and branch `<build-branch>--s<n>` from the build branch, and when the step is done, merge it back into the build branch under the store lock. A merge conflict sends the step back as `blocked` with a note and re-runs it after the steps it clashed with.

Step-scoped launches: let deploy/claude-headless.sh take `--step <id>`. The brief then carries only that step, its `dependsOn` results and the files it touches. Each step books its own agent slot through agent-slots.mjs, and model-gate is checked per step.

Dispatcher: change `pipeline.mjs tick` to call planFill every minute and launch everything it returns until the slots or accounts run out. Record each launch on the build (step `runningIn`, session and worktree) through builds-live. A crashed step goes back to ready, with at most 3 runs.

Auto-queue pending: when `builds.autoQueuePending` is on and slots are left after every ready step and Queue build has one, move split Pending builds that have no clashes to the Queue in priority order, with a build note (`auto-queued: slots free`) and one alert through axf.notify@1 (declared in notify.json).

Reconciler: teach builds-reconcile.mjs about parallel steps, so a step session that is not alive is reset to ready with its worktree kept, and a build counts as `built` only when every step branch has merged back.

agent-slots: add a `fill` view that shows free slots and what planFill would launch next (dry run), and make the idle alert ('nothing running while the Queue has work') also fire when there are free slots and ready steps.

REST API: add build-orchestrator routes GET /pipeline/fill (state: slots, ready steps, the plan, settings), POST /pipeline/fill/run (one tick now), POST /builds/:id/steps/:step/deps (set dependsOn), POST /pipeline/settings (fillSlots and maxParallelPerBuild; autoQueuePending is refused unless Brett's own session sends it).

Make the same actions available through MCP, the CLI and voice: plugin commands pipeline-fill-status, pipeline-fill-run, pipeline-step-deps and pipeline-fill-settings; `pipeline.mjs fill status|run|deps|set`; AmberX voice actions with the same names. All four go through one shared handler.

Pipeline tab UI: add a Slots strip (one chip per slot: which build and step runs there, or free) and a badge on each build showing 'N steps running in parallel'. Use framework controls and tokens only, a TabGroup or toolbar with role=toolbar and a settings id.

Step dependency view: in the build detail, list each step's dependsOn with an editor (a multi-select of earlier steps) and show the state (ready, waiting on, running in slot N). Wire it to POST /steps/:step/deps.

Settings sub-tab (Settings → Plugins → Build orchestrator): Fill every slot, Max parallel steps per build, Auto-queue pending builds (owner-only, greyed out for sessions), with the level toolbar. Add console_show deep links `builds/pipeline/slots`, `builds/<id>/steps` and `settings/plugins/build-orchestrator#fill`.

Help and glossary: add descriptions for the new commands, routes, settings and CLI to the plugin help and to _claude/builds/README.md (Pipeline: fill every slot). Run glossary-index catalog.mjs --check.

Tests: dispatcher integration test with a fake claude (HOME/.local/bin) and 4 slots running two builds, one a DAG. Check that the steps fill the slots, a clash is held back, the step branches merge back and auto-queue only fires when the setting is on. Also run test.py for the routes, including the owner-only refusal.

UI Review: take shots of the Slots strip, step deps and settings on desktop and phone (vite preview with /api/me mocked), with 3 options as assets (strip layouts) in plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/, and submit through review.mjs.

Final: run check-build-pipeline-fill, check-builds-store, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets and the plugin lifecycle check. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/always-fill-every-slot-when-slots-are-free-run-independent-steps-of-running-bu.md, add the THREADS.md row, link the branch, and open the PR saying how each feature is reached (deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice) and that UI Review is waiting.
